report.headline: stripe/terraform-provider-stripe runs a fast, disciplined human engineering process — quick reviews, working CI, schema-synced docs — but has not yet adopted any AI-native conventions, agentic workflows, or test automation, placing it at the Manual/Assisted boundary (L1-L2) despite otherwise healthy practices.
strengths: Fast, disciplined PR velocity (median 1.3h to merge, 1.1h to first review) with 83% of merges carrying an approving review and 0% reverted.
Working CI (2 GitHub Actions workflows enforcing gofmt and go vet) plus a branch-protection ruleset on main.
Extensive, schema-synced documentation — a 25-section README with a working quickstart, auto-generated /docs/resources and /docs/data-sources trees, and an examples directory.
An internal code-generation pipeline already produces resource/datasource code from a spec, showing existing appetite for automation even though it isn't yet AI-driven.
Dependabot is already active in the dependency-update flow, a plausible first hook toward broader automation.
risks: Zero machine-readable AI guidance (no CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md) means any AI assistant working in this repo has no shared context on build/test/release commands or conventions, so contribution quality will vary session to session.

No detected test suite for a payments-infrastructure provider is a significant correctness risk — recent history shows multiple hand-fixed regressions (decimal drift, missing computed fields, nested-block IDs) that a test suite typically exists to catch, especially before trusting AI-authored changes to CRUD/schema logic.
Branch protection on main is nominal only (0 required approvals, no required status checks), so the CI checks and reviews that do happen today aren't structurally enforced gates.

No SAST, no committed dependency-update automation, minimal Action pinning (4/12 by SHA), and no artifact signing/SBOM leave meaningful supply-chain exposure for a Stripe-authored infrastructure tool.
No AI-in-CI, no AI review bots, and a measured 0% AI-involved PR rate mean any AI adoption today is invisible and informal, with nothing systemized for the team to build on.
